observations.context: Unfinished bead in Trench38 bead pot
observations.source_observation: An unfinished carnelian bead has a tubular perforation.
observations.source_author_inference: Caption suggests later bead workshops and changed drilling technology.
observations.current_inference: A working stage is represented on the object; mixed collection must constrain its manufacture attribution.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Imported roughout, curated earlier unfinished object and local work all remain possible without associated waste/tools.
observations.lineage: HARP 1996 Trench 38 bead-pot context

observations.context: Same unfinished bead
observations.source_observation: The caption describes unusual color and a different drilling form.
observations.source_author_inference: Color is interpreted as a non-Gujarat source and drilling as response to lost specialized-stone supply.
observations.current_inference: Separate a proposed supply explanation from observed form.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Color can change with treatment; geological source, drill material and supply interruption were not directly established in the inspected caption.
observations.lineage: HARP 1996 Trench 38 bead-pot context

observations.locus: Prose and final unique substantive image-alt caption
observations.context: Trench38 small pot and its 133 decorative objects
observations.phase: Pot assigned around1700BCE; contents from multiple phases
observations.source_observation: The description says the pot's contents belong to all Harappan occupation phases.
observations.source_author_inference: A bead collector retained diverse objects.
observations.current_inference: Deposition of the collection cannot assign one manufacture date to each object.
observations.limits_and_rivals: The same context as MO01–MO02 is not independent replication.
observations.lineage: HARP 1996 Trench 38 bead-pot context

observations.locus: Printed p.209/PDF p.3, Table2 and adjacent chronology
observations.context: Period5 carbon sample H1999/9803[410]
observations.source_observation: Table2 reports a Period5 calibrated range of 1880–1680BCE at its stated at-least90% probability scope.
observations.source_author_inference: Cemetery H phase was established by approximately1700calBCE; terminal date remains poorly preserved.
observations.current_inference: An intermediate settlement phase has dating support.
observations.limits_and_rivals: The carbon context is not a direct bead-manufacture date or a verified association with the selected pot.
observations.lineage: HARP Harappa excavation programme

observations.context: Harappa phase framework
observations.source_observation: The earlier framework leaves a terminal bound extending below1300BCE; the later framework and discussion leave the endpoint unresolved.
observations.source_author_inference: Continuing chronological refinement.
observations.current_inference: A phase table does not provide a fixed duration for technical transmission.
observations.limits_and_rivals: MS07–MS08 share excavation ancestry and are not two confirmations of one date.
observations.lineage: HARP Harappa excavation programme

observations.context: Hulas PeriodI pottery
observations.source_observation: Striations, separate neck/body joining and trimming are described, with sand/lime/husk temper and surface finishing.
observations.source_author_inference: Wheel forming, luting and finishing are reconstructed; firing method remains unclear.
observations.current_inference: The report preserves a linked manufacture candidate beyond vessel names.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Finished pots can travel; these generic operations do not identify maker ancestry or a local teaching chain.
observations.lineage: ASI Hulas 1978–1983 excavation and associated botanical sample

observations.context: Hulas potsherds and burnt plaster carrying plant impressions
observations.source_observation: Rice-husk impressions occur in potsherds and burnt mud-plaster pieces.
observations.source_author_inference: Husk was used as clay temper and interpreted as an agricultural by-product.
observations.current_inference: Candidate connection between plant handling and construction/craft material preparation.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Deliberate addition, processing location and cultivation require controls against naturally included plant material, imported crops and wild collection.
observations.lineage: ASI Hulas 1978–1983 excavation and associated botanical sample

observations.context: Rice impressions and cited clay-source alternative
observations.source_observation: The author discusses the difficulty separating wild/cultivated rice from impressions and the possibility of rice-bearing marsh clay.
observations.source_author_inference: Hulas rice cultivation is favored in the subsequent argument.
observations.current_inference: Presence of an impression does not decide cultivation or a transmission route.
observations.limits_and_rivals: The marsh-clay discussion initially addresses comparative Gujarat cases; applying it to Hulas is a prospective formation control, not an excavated Hulas fact.
observations.lineage: ASI Hulas 1978–1983 excavation and associated botanical sample

observations.context: Botanical soil samples from one field season
observations.source_observation: Visible remains and water separation through a25-mesh sieve recovered material around0.7mm; carbonization damaged identification. The study used one season's sample.
observations.source_author_inference: Recognizable remains approximate part of plant use.
observations.current_inference: Recovery, burning and aggregation constrain operation comparisons.
observations.limits_and_rivals: No standardized yield, same-field rotation or independent-trial seed count is inferred.
observations.lineage: ASI Hulas 1978–1983 excavation and associated botanical sample

observations.context: Hulas site and separately placed period areas
observations.source_observation: The appendix's typological circa1700–1000BCE attribution differs from main discussion of much earlier uncalibrated dates; the later PGW occupation is in a different part of the mound.
observations.source_author_inference: Authors offer different broad regional phase interpretations.
observations.current_inference: Hulas is a source-reported intermediate candidate with unresolved precise dating and succession.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Do not join phases into uninterrupted same-household learning or adopt the older river-event dating argument.
observations.lineage: ASI Hulas 1978–1983 excavation and associated botanical sample

observations.context: Hulas walnut and almond remains
observations.observation_kind: source botanical record and ecological interpretation
observations.source_observation: Walnut and almond remains are described.
observations.source_author_inference: Ecological distribution is used to propose distant supply.
observations.current_inference: Imported food is a plausible component of the assemblage.
observations.limits_and_rivals: A food taxon's presence does not locate the knowledge or field that produced it; trade route and elite status are not independently observed.
observations.lineage: ASI Hulas 1978–1983 excavation and associated botanical sample

observations.context: BPR-36 from a late level of Sub-periodIB
observations.source_observation: The catalogue identifies a roughly faceted unfinished black-jasper bead.
observations.source_author_inference: Unfinished beads and raw material support proposed bead making at the site.
observations.current_inference: The later assemblage contains a source-qualified working-stage object rather than only completed ornaments.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Imported/curated roughouts and movement of craftspeople remain rivals; associated waste/tools and exact date are not supplied here.

observations.context: BPR-208, mid-level Sub-periodIB
observations.source_observation: BPR-208 is described as unfinished quartz in one list and unfinished banded agate in another.
observations.source_author_inference: Both entries place it in mid-IB.
observations.current_inference: Retain one accession-level record pending object verification.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Do not count two independent specimens or resolve the material by preference.
observations.lineage: ASI Bhagwanpura 1975–1976 excavation and selected scientific specimens

observations.locus: Printed p.30/PDF p.55, Arts and Crafts
observations.context: Bhagwanpura craft assemblage
observations.source_observation: Unfinished beads, raw material and pottery dabbers are reported.
observations.source_author_inference: The authors infer bead making and local pottery manufacture.
observations.current_inference: Production is a testable local working hypothesis.
observations.limits_and_rivals: No complete linked waste/tool sequence or observed teacher relation appears in this locus; broad local transmission and regional transfer both fit.
observations.lineage: ASI Bhagwanpura 1975–1976 excavation and selected scientific specimens

observations.context: Grey/red pottery forms
observations.source_observation: Some grey-ware shapes resemble the Late Harappan bowls, jars, basins and dishes-on-stand.
observations.source_author_inference: The authors describe copying and interaction between potters.
observations.current_inference: Opportunity for transfer is compatible with the forms.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Shared function, imports and convergence remain; the forms are not calibrated as rare technical signatures.
observations.lineage: ASI Bhagwanpura 1975–1976 excavation and selected scientific specimens

observations.context: Twelve selected pottery specimens
observations.phase: Individual phase/findspot joins not supplied in inspected analysis
observations.source_observation: Bulk composition, sections and physical properties are compared across differently colored sherds; wheel manufacture is reported.
observations.source_author_inference: Tandon proposes similar source clay and different thermal conditions.
observations.current_inference: Raw-body and firing choices are separate comparison dimensions.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Bulk similarity without geological controls cannot establish local provenance; mixed unidentified phases do not yield a dated recipe succession.
observations.lineage: ASI Bhagwanpura 1975–1976 excavation and selected scientific specimens

observations.context: Four saddle querns and pestles on a hut floor
observations.source_observation: Grinding tools occur together on a hut floor; the report says grains were not recovered at Bhagwanpura.
observations.source_author_inference: A grain-grinder's household and flour/paste making are proposed.
observations.current_inference: A bounded working-place candidate is more informative than generic farming labels.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Use residues and wear are needed to distinguish grain from other grinding; this does not observe sowing, ploughing or irrigation.
observations.lineage: ASI Bhagwanpura 1975–1976 excavation and selected scientific specimens

observations.context: Local stratigraphic sequence and flood horizons
observations.source_observation: The report describes no stratigraphic break at the transition and changing associated wares after flood episodes.
observations.source_author_inference: It identifies interacting cultural populations and proposed learning.
observations.current_inference: Local contact is an opportunity hypothesis requiring technical and person-level evidence.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Pottery labels do not identify language/ethnicity; flood mixing and changing use need local context checks.
observations.lineage: ASI Bhagwanpura 1975–1976 excavation and selected scientific specimens

observations.locus: TL chapter p.185 andTable6 p.201/PDF pp.231,247
observations.context: Pottery dates and depth series
observations.source_observation: TL analysis reports broad errors and different depth trends for grey and red pottery; its BP table uses1978 as measurement date.
observations.source_author_inference: Water-content variation is a major dating uncertainty.
observations.current_inference: The source cannot supply a precise instruction interval or one date for every artifact.

observations.locus: Printed p.3/PDF p.12, Late Harappan section
observations.context: Bara domestic phases
observations.source_observation: Mud-walled rooms, circular bins and hearths occur in the reported Bara sequence.
observations.source_author_inference: Bins are described as corn storage.
observations.current_inference: Repeated household material tasks supply possible carrier settings.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Contents, use residues and transmission between occupants are not measured; room size is not converted to population.
observations.lineage: ASI and Punjab archaeology Sanghol 1986–1987 excavation

observations.context: Sanghol phase association and later factory claim
observations.source_observation: The SGL9 overlap list marks PGW with a question mark and notes levelling; the bead/terracotta factory suggestion concerns Kushana buildings.
observations.source_author_inference: Further exposure is requested to establish overlap.
observations.current_inference: Keep possible overlap and later production at different dates.
observations.limits_and_rivals: A Kushana factory does not demonstrate an intermediate Late Harappan workshop; phase co-occurrence is not teaching.

observations.context: Jognakhera YA1/IV layers5–12; eight botanical samples
observations.source_observation: Eight0.5mm-flotation samples contain crops, legumes and weeds, with context codes inTableS1.
observations.source_author_inference: Winter and summer crops are treated as a continuing farming package.
observations.current_inference: The later regional plant-use sequence has specified recovery and contextual observations.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Aggregated counts do not observe same-plot cultivation, a teacher or an independently traced origin.
observations.lineage: Jognakhera YA1/IV botanical samples and three new grain dates

observations.context: Three newly dated Jognakhera crop specimens
observations.source_observation: Source-calibrated ranges are barley2471–2298, Vigna1880–1691 andrice1517–1428calBCE at95.4% scope.
observations.source_author_inference: These dates anchor a broad cultural sequence.
observations.current_inference: The study adds directly dated second-millennium crop-use observations.
observations.limits_and_rivals: TableS2 gives site-level context rather than each sampled-layer join. Date a specimen, not an uninterrupted farming/teaching sequence.
observations.lineage: Jognakhera YA1/IV botanical samples and three new grain dates

observations.context: Congealed rice-husk mass and recovered legumes
observations.phase: Sampled deposits; individual residue date unresolved
observations.source_observation: A congealed husk mass is illustrated and named, alongside cereal and legume remains.
observations.source_author_inference: The crop pattern is interpreted as double cropping and rotation.
observations.current_inference: A processing-stage residue can be targeted for an operation comparison.
observations.limits_and_rivals: The mass does not establish the sequence of husking, its place in cultivation or source of the food; crop co-presence does not identify rotation.
observations.lineage: Jognakhera YA1/IV botanical samples and three new grain dates

observations.context: Crop-package and geographic comparison
observations.source_observation: The article compares regional crop/ceramic patterns and directly dated rice.
observations.source_author_inference: Rotation, eastward migration and cultural continuity are proposed.
observations.current_inference: Separate availability of a regional package from its carrier and transmission route.
observations.limits_and_rivals: Imports, contact, varied fields and similar ecological solutions remain; river identity and population migration are not identified by the plant sample.
observations.lineage: Jognakhera YA1/IV botanical samples and three new grain dates

observations.context: Early Ravi living surfaces, pits/hearths and screened debris
observations.source_observation: Jasper drills, agate flakes and unfinished beads were recovered from associated living surfaces with systematic screening and microstratigraphy.
observations.source_author_inference: An early bead-making area is reconstructed.
observations.current_inference: This shows the kind of association needed to strengthen the later working-stage candidates.
observations.limits_and_rivals: The control is thousands of years earlier and is not an intermediate bridging observation.
